planning_notes: Preserve given wiring: D13 -> 220Ω resistor -> LED (LED anode side), and Arduino GND -> LED cathode. D2 -> pushbutton node (button connected between D2 and GND). Internal INPUT pull-up is assumed because the prose says reads LOW when pressed using pull-up resistor configuration.
Button model normalization: model=true means pressed; this is achieved with active_high=false on the digital_input so LOW at the pin maps to model true.
Control step updates outputs every control_period_ms; LED mirrors button pressed state without any additional timing logic.
No serial reporting, sensors, displays, PWM, servo, tone, or other devices are present in the provided circuit.

interfaces.name: io_0
interfaces.meaning: LED command (ON only while button pressed). Button pressed reads LOW; LED true when pressed, so active_high=true is required.

interfaces.name: io_1
interfaces.meaning: Pushbutton state; reads LOW when pressed (INPUT uses pull-up so unpressed is HIGH). Model value is true when pressed.

# Button Controlled LED

## Project Description
This is a Arduino project that controls an LED with a pushbutton. The LED will turn on only while the button is pressed and turn off when released.

## Hardware Components
- Arduino Uno
- Push Button
- 220Ω resistor
- LED

## Circuit Description
The circuit consists of:
- A pushbutton connected to a digital pin.
- An LED connected to a digital output pin through a 220Ω current-limiting resistor
- The cathode (negative leg) of the LED is connected to ground

## Expected Behavior
When the Arduino powers up, it should:
1. Configure the button pin as INPUT
2. Configure the LED pin as OUTPUT
3. Continuously monitor the button state
4. Turn the LED ON when the button is pressed (reads LOW)
5. Turn the LED OFF when the button is released (reads HIGH)

## Success Criteria
The test is successful when:
1. The LED turns on immediately when the button is pressed
2. The LED remains on only while the button is held down
3. The LED turns off immediately when the button is released

## Notes for Implementation
- The button input will read LOW when pressed if using a pull-up resistor configuration
- Ensure proper current-limiting resistor for the LED based on its specifications
- When the button is not pressed, pin1.l is connected to pin1.r and pin2.l is connected to pin2.r. When the button is pressed, all the pins are connected together.

## Attributes
- To use 220Ω resistor, set the property name "value" to "220 ohm".
Given circuit (must preserve wiring):
{
    "version": 1.0,
    "author": "Blind Author",
    "editor": "Blind Author",
    "description": "Button LED",
    "parts": [
        {
            "id": "arduino uno1",
            "type": "wokwi-arduino-uno",
            "top": 200,
            "left": 20
        },
        {
            "id": "resistor1",
            "type": "wokwi-resistor",
            "top": 75,
            "left": 115,
            "rotate": 90,
            "attrs": {
                "value": "220"
            }
        },
        {
            "id": "push button1",
            "type": "wokwi-pushbutton",
            "top": 125,
            "left": 180,
            "rotate": 90
        },
        {
            "id": "led1",
            "type": "wokwi-led",
            "left": 120,
            "top": 0,
            "attrs": {
                "color": "red"
            }
        }
    ],
    "connections": [
        [
            "arduino uno1:GND.1",
            "led1:C",
            "black",
            []
        ],
        [
            "resistor1:1",
            "led1:A",
            "green",
            []
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:13",
            "resistor1:2",
            "green",
            [
                "*",
                "h0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:2",
            "push button1:1.r",
            "red",
            [
                "v-12",
                "*",
                "h0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:GND.1",
            "push button1:2.l",
            "red",
            [
                "v-95",
                "*",
                "h0"
            ]
        ]
    ]
}
